name: RelayDB
title: RelayDB Universal 4-Tag Memory Compiler
summary: RelayDB compiles tagged JSON or JSONL source memory into a verified .relay artifact that can be navigated by anchor and relationship links.
source_truth: Generated after successful JSONL -> .relay build, verify, and jump tests.

title: RelayDB Self-Documentation Loop
summary: RelayDB can document itself by converting its own code structure and design decisions into tagged JSONL, compiling that memory into a .relay file, and using that .relay file as a documentation/data source.
pipeline: Project facts are authored as tagged JSONL records.
RelayDB compiler ingests the JSONL file.
relay jump navigates the compiled project memory.
A documentation site or AI assistant can consume the same .relay memory.

title: Tagged JSONL Source Memory
summary: RelayDB source memory is authored as JSONL, where each line is a standalone JSON object representing a project node.
rules: Each JSONL line must be a valid JSON object.
Each node should have a stable anchor in the # field.
The ^ field stores provenance or upstream source relationships.
The @ field stores related project nodes.
The ~ field stores aliases and retrieval terms.

tags.^: provenance, source, parent, or upstream context
tags.@: relationships, links, edges, affected nodes, or related concepts
tags.~: aliases, search terms, alternate names, retrieval hints

title: Compiled .relay Artifact
summary: A .relay file is the compiled output of RelayDB. It stores serialized JSON node payloads and a jump table that maps anchors to byte offsets.
important_distinction: RelayDB currently compiles and minifies structured memory; it does not perform general-purpose compression.

title: .relay Binary Format
summary: The .relay artifact uses a reserved header, serialized JSON payload blocks, null terminators, and a jump-table pointer.
layout: Write JSON node payloads as minified JSON bytes.
Append a null terminator after each node payload.
Write a jump table at the end of the file.
Write the jump-table byte offset into the header at byte 16 as little-endian u64.

name: POINTER_START
summary: Byte offset in the .relay header where the jump-table pointer is stored.

name: HEADER_SIZE
summary: Number of bytes reserved at the start of a .relay file for header data.

name: TERMINATOR
summary: Null byte written after each serialized JSON node payload.

name: relay_compiler
summary: Shared library for RelayDB protocol constants, tag extraction, .relay reading, integrity checking, recursive traversal, display formatting, and node writing.

name: extract_anchor_id
summary: Returns a stable anchor ID for a JSON node. Supports both RelayDB legacy #id anchors and ATLAS-style # anchors.

name: extract_links_from_node
summary: Shared relationship extractor used to collect links from @ and ^ tagged fields. Handles both string values and arrays of strings.

title: RelayDB Relationship Graph
summary: RelayDB treats tagged JSON fields as graph edges. The compiler uses extracted links for topology/audit artifacts, while runtime traversal follows @ relationship links.
rules: ^ links represent provenance or upstream context.
The compiler may warn about cycles because project-memory graphs can be relational rather than strictly acyclic.
Runtime traversal uses a visited set to prevent infinite recursion.

title: Universal Compiler
summary: RelayDB v1.2 accepts configurable input and output paths and supports both .json and .jsonl source files.
capabilities: Compile a directory containing .json and .jsonl files.
Generate audit artifacts in a configurable builds directory.

name: compiler
summary: Command-line compiler that ingests JSON/JSONL source memory, builds graph analysis, warns or fails on cycles depending on mode, generates audit artifacts, and writes a .relay file.

cli_args.--input: Input file or directory containing .json or .jsonl files.
cli_args.--strict-acyclic: Fail build if relationship graph contains cycles.

name: ingest_data
summary: Builds GraphAnalysis by collecting supported input files, reading JSON/JSONL nodes, extracting anchors, and extracting relationship links.

name: collect_input_files
summary: Collects supported .json and .jsonl files from either a single input file or a directory.
side_effects: reads directory entries when input path is a directory

name: is_supported_data_file
summary: Returns true for paths ending in .json or .jsonl.

name: read_nodes_from_file
summary: Dispatches file parsing to either read_json_nodes or read_jsonl_nodes depending on file extension.

name: read_json_nodes
summary: Reads a .json file containing either a JSON object or an array of JSON objects.

name: read_jsonl_nodes
summary: Reads a .jsonl file where each non-empty line must be a JSON object.
error_behavior: Reports invalid JSON with file and line number.
Rejects JSONL lines that are not objects.

name: GraphAnalysis
summary: Compiler data structure containing parsed nodes and an adjacency list of extracted relationships.

name: verify_no_cycles
summary: Checks the relationship graph for cycles. In v1.2, cycles warn by default and only fail the build when --strict-acyclic is enabled.

name: has_cycle
summary: Depth-first search helper for cycle detection using visited and recursion-stack sets.

title: Strict Acyclic Mode
summary: Optional compiler mode that fails the build if any relationship cycle is detected. It is off by default because project-memory graphs commonly contain valid semantic cycles.

name: generate_artifacts
summary: Writes a Markdown audit report and delegates DOT graph generation.

name: generate_dot_file
summary: Writes a generic Graphviz DOT representation of the relationship graph without hardcoded Bacon Standard categories.

title: Audit Artifacts
summary: The compiler produces human-readable audit artifacts alongside the .relay file.

name: bake_binary
summary: Creates the output .relay file, reserves header space, writes node payloads, writes a tab-separated jump table, and writes the jump-table pointer into the header.

name: solder_node
summary: Serializes a JSON node into minified JSON bytes, writes it to the .relay file, appends the null terminator, and returns the node's starting byte position.

title: Jump Table
summary: The jump table maps each anchor to the byte offset of that node's payload in the .relay artifact.
reason_for_tab_separator: Anchors may contain colons, such as function:fetch_entry, so tab separation avoids ambiguity.

name: get_address_from
summary: Finds the byte offset for an anchor in a chosen .relay file by reading the jump-table pointer and scanning jump-table entries.
complexity_note: Current implementation scans the jump table linearly before performing the byte jump.

name: fetch_entry_from
summary: Reads a JSON payload from a chosen .relay file starting at a byte offset until the null terminator is reached.

name: get_jump_table_from
summary: Reads all jump-table entries from a chosen .relay file and returns anchor-offset pairs.

name: verify_integrity_from
summary: Verifies a chosen .relay file by checking that every jump-table anchor points to a JSON payload with a matching # or #id anchor.

title: Physical Integrity Check
summary: RelayDB verifies that every jump-table entry points to the correct serialized node payload.
successful_test_observed: The relaydb-docs.relay artifact passed make verify after compilation.

name: relay_jump_from
summary: Recursively navigates a chosen .relay file starting from an anchor, displays matching nodes, follows @ links, and uses a visited set to avoid infinite recursion.

title: Recursive Jump Traversal
summary: RelayDB can start at one anchor and recursively follow @ links through the compiled graph.
rules: The starting anchor is looked up in the jump table.
The node payload is fetched by byte offset.
The node is displayed if it passes the optional filter.
A visited set prevents infinite loops.

name: process_baton
summary: Processes @ baton values during runtime traversal. Supports string links and arrays of string links.

name: should_display_entry
summary: Display filter used during relay jumps. Without a filter it displays entries; with a filter it checks whether the serialized node contains the filter string.

name: display_formatted_entry
summary: Formats a node for terminal display using tag-aware labels for anchors, provenance, aliases, relay links, and normal data.
side_effects: prints formatted node fields to stdout

name: relay
summary: Universal RelayDB command-line interface with check and jump subcommands that accept a chosen .relay file.

commands.check: Verify physical integrity of a .relay file.
commands.jump: Navigate from an anchor in a .relay file.

name: reader
summary: Simple demonstration reader. The universal workflow should prefer the relay CLI for custom files and anchors.

name: verify
summary: Standalone integrity inspector that accepts a .relay file argument and delegates validation to verify_integrity_from.

title: Documentation Repair Loop
summary: Missing anchor warnings identify referenced nodes that do not yet exist in source memory. These warnings can drive the next JSONL patch.
observed_missing_anchor_types: ATLAS concepts referenced but not included
external concepts intentionally outside the current memory set
workflow: Decide whether each missing anchor should become a node or be marked external.

title: Missing Anchor Warning
summary: A missing anchor warning occurs when a node references an anchor that is not present in the compiled jump table.
meaning: The relationship points to a node that is not currently included in the memory artifact.
not_always_bad: Some missing anchors may be intentional external references, but internal project references should usually be added as nodes.

title: External Reference Policy
summary: Some @ or ^ references may intentionally point outside the current .relay memory artifact. These should be marked or handled clearly so warnings do not look like errors.
possible_future_rule: Add an external flag or external: prefix for references that should not be resolved inside the current artifact.

title: Stale Source Memory
summary: Compiled memory is only as accurate as the JSONL source. After refactoring RelayDB, old records may still describe previous behavior.
observed_examples: Records from the first test JSONL still mentioned bacon_standard.relay.
Records from the first test JSONL still described hardcoded Bacon Standard visualization categories.
Records from the first test JSONL still documented risks that have now been partially fixed.
mitigation: Generate a clean v1 JSONL memory file after code refactors.
Use missing-anchor warnings and stale descriptions as inputs for the next memory patch.
Treat compiled .relay output as a release artifact generated from reviewed source memory.

title: Linear Jump Table Scan
summary: Current anchor lookup scans the text jump table linearly before seeking to the target byte offset.
impact: Lookup is not true O(1) yet. The byte seek is direct after the anchor is found, but anchor lookup is O(n) over jump-table entries.
future_mitigation: Load jump table into an in-memory HashMap.
Use a sorted binary index and binary search.
Compile a fixed-width offset index for direct lookup.

title: Use .relay as the Compiled Project Memory Artifact
summary: Use .relay as the compiled memory artifact instead of introducing a separate .aihd file extension for the MVP.
reason: RelayDB already compiles tagged JSONL memory into a navigable artifact. Keeping .relay avoids an extra file type and keeps the MVP simpler.

title: Allow Relationship Cycles by Default
summary: The universal compiler warns about cycles but continues by default because project-memory graphs are relational and often validly cyclic.
reason: A function can point to a concept and that concept can point back to the function. That is useful memory, not corruption.

title: Support Both JSON and JSONL Source Inputs
summary: The compiler supports .json object files, .json array files, and .jsonl line-delimited object files.
reason: JSONL is append-friendly and works well for branch memory and documentation patches, while JSON remains useful for existing data files.

title: Use Tab-Separated Jump Table Entries
summary: Jump-table entries use anchor<TAB>offset so anchors may safely contain colons.
reason: ATLAS-style anchors often use names like function:fetch_entry or risk:stale-source-memory. Colon-separated jump table parsing would be ambiguous.

title: RelayDB Docs Build Verify Jump Test
summary: A JSONL memory file with 42 nodes was compiled into relaydb-docs.relay, verified successfully, and navigated with project and risk anchors.
result: Compiler warned about a cycle but continued.
Jump traversal returned project memory and linked nodes.
